title: Feedback on a wheelie game, and three wishes answered in 21 minutes
summary: On Tue 17 Nov @eriskii.net posted "holy shit" over an image with no description (205 likes); replies describe a video of a skid-steer loader doing wheelies. Four and a half hours later @cee.wtf quote-posted it with a browser game: "do a sick wheelie at yard-shift.cee.wtf" (122 likes, 15 reposts). Six minutes after that @tvanl.bsky.social gave feedback that the left and right controls sit too close together on a phone; @cee.wtf awarded themself the "didnt even consider people on mobile" award "once again", and got the reply "I can't bring my desktop in my forklift". At 00:10Z @shimmermathlabs.com listed three wishes: skid marks, a driver who can hang off the edge or jump out, and a button for hoots and woots. At 00:31Z @cee.wtf replied "done" with a screenshot. Her answering screenshot, by its alt text, shows the loader tipped back on its rear wheels, skid marks on the ground, a worker hanging off the side and a "Woot!" message.

posts.alt: Screenshot from a cartoony 3D construction game. A yellow skid steer loader with a black frame and a caged cab is tipped back onto its rear wheels, nose in the air, its arms fully extended so the bucket is up overhead. Two loose wheels sit in the bucket. A small worker in an orange high-vis vest and yellow hard hat hangs off the side of the machine, one arm flung up as if cheering or falling. A little “Woot!” message floats at the top of the screen. The setting is a concrete yard with tire skid marks, a chain-link fence and rounded low-poly trees under a gray sky.

sensitive: No post on this card carries a flag from the tool. (1) The game is a made thing and belongs to the made lane; this card is the exchange under it. @cee.wtf also holds the Top Chicken record and won Saturday's result, so the games lane will name them too: three lanes may carry the same account. (2) The post the game quotes drew replies the tool flags (health) and a link to an outside news story about the video; none of that is here, and the outside story is not the cluster's. (3) "people with big thumbs" is the poster's remark about their own hands (appearance, lightly). "my forklift" may be about the poster's job (R1): not known, see notUnderstood. (4) "there has to be a way to run yourself over" is about the game's driver character. (5) @shimmermathlabs.com is marked by the tool as shown in the previous episode, and appears on four cards in this lane. (6) @tvanl.bsky.social has 785 followers.
